description: The figure contains two stacked line plots that illustrate how two quantities, labeled \(n\) (top) and \(Size_{run}\) (bottom), vary as a function of \(m\). In both plots, the x-axis is labeled \(m\), uses a linear scale, starts at 0 at the left, and extends to the right without numeric tick labels; a vertical dashed reference line marks a specific position labeled \(m_0\). In the top plot, the y-axis is labeled \(n\), uses a linear scale, and shows labeled reference levels including 0 at the baseline and horizontal dashed lines at \(w\), \(c-a-s\), and \(c-a\). A single black solid line with no markers forms a repeating sawtooth: it rises linearly from near 0 up to the dashed level at \(c-a\), then drops abruptly down to the dashed level at \(w\), and repeats this rise-and-drop pattern multiple times across increasing \(m\); the sawtooth continues past the vertical marker at \(m_0\) with similar triangular ramps and sharp downward resets. In the bottom plot, the y-axis is labeled \(Size_{run}\), uses a linear scale, and includes labeled reference levels with 0 at the baseline and horizontal dashed lines at \(w+a+s\) and \(c\), with an additional label \(a\) shown near the top of the axis. A single black solid line with no markers again forms a sawtooth pattern: it increases linearly from 0 up to the dashed level at \(c\), then drops sharply to a lower level, after which it repeats cycles that rise to peaks near the upper portion of the axis and then fall abruptly to troughs aligned with the dashed level at \(w+a+s\); these repeated ramps and drops continue across \(m\), including to the right of the vertical dashed line at \(m_0\).
caption_used: The line plots depict the evolution of two key numerical metrics—n (top) and Size_run (bottom)—as a function of the variable m, illustrating dynamic cache behavior in a streaming context. The x-axis, labeled m, progresses from 0 to a terminal value without explicit numerical markers. The y-axis of the top plot is segmented by horizontal dashed lines at c-a, c-a-s, and w, with the solid black line exhibiting a sawtooth pattern: it ascends linearly to approximately 60 units above the baseline before sharply declining to w, then repeating this cyclical rise-and-fall trajectory, intersecting the m_0 threshold at each trough. The bottom plot, labeled Size_run, mirrors this structure with dashed lines at c, w+a+s, and a. Here, the black line rises steadily to c, then collapses abruptly to the baseline before resuming a sawtooth pattern, with peaks consistently exceeding the c threshold by roughly 25% and troughs stabilizing at w+a+s. Notably, the amplitude of fluctuations in the bottom plot diminishes progressively after the m_0 intercept, suggesting a convergence toward equilibrium. Comparative analysis reveals that the top plot’s sawtooth cycles maintain a uniform amplitude, whereas the bottom plot’s cycles demonstrate a marked reduction in variability over time.
